en.title: Stress on the Third-Last Syllable
en.summary: Learn how to find and pronounce stress on the third-last syllable in Romanian words.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: You count syllables from the end of a word. In some words, you stress the third-last syllable. Listen to (muzică) /ˈmu.zi.kə/, which means music. Your voice climbs and sounds stronger on that part. The remaining syllables drop in power. This pattern gives long words a lively rhythm.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Open your mouth clearly on the stressed vowel. Push more air from your lungs. Make that syllable louder and slightly longer. Let your pitch rise a little bit. Then, relax your mouth for the final syllables. Do not stop the air between the parts. Keep the sound flowing smoothly to the very end.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look at long words with care. Many words place the stress near the end. Notice the word (fotografie) /fo.to.ɡraˈfi.e/, which means photograph. Here, the strong beat lands near the end. However, other words pull the beat back to the third-last syllable. Listen closely to each word to learn its beat.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not stress every syllable with equal force. Give only one syllable the main beat. Do not push the stress too far forward. In (fotografie) /fo.to.ɡraˈfi.e/, keep the force on the correct part. Do not drop the final vowels completely. Keep your tongue relaxed and speak without rushing.
